I'd be very cautious here, because in many states RNs can't legally inject Botox without a supervising physician or medical director, and house parties typically lack proper sterile conditions and emergency equipment. If something goes wrong, you could lose your nursing license and face liability that your employer's malpractice coverage won't touch. If aesthetics interests you, check your state board of nursing's rules and look into working at a licensed medspa with proper oversight and your own malpractice insurance.
Manager offered me a promotion with a new title but no raise. Take it?

A title without pay is worth questioning, so thank them and ask directly what the compensation adjustment will be for the expanded role. If budget is truly frozen, get a written commitment to revisit salary on a specific date, plus any immediate perks they can offer. The title can still help your resume, but don't let it quietly become more work for the same money.
can i pay my car loan with a credit card to get the rewards

Most auto lenders don't accept credit cards, and those that do often charge a fee that wipes out the rewards. Third-party payment services also charge fees, usually around 2.5 to 3 percent, which is more than most cards earn back. Unless you're using it briefly to hit a sign-up bonus and can pay the card off in full right away, it isn't worth it.
Got 35k inheritance. Girlfriend wants to use it for our wedding. Thoughts?

That's a values question as much as a money one, so talk openly about what each of you wants your life to look like in five years. Spending some on the wedding is reasonable, but consider capping it and putting the rest toward an emergency fund, debt, or a house down payment, which will likely matter more over time. Also know that inheritances are often treated as separate property, so if you mix it into joint accounts, it can change how it's treated legally.
My kid got a full scholarship! Now what do I do with the $60k in the 529?

Congratulations! You can withdraw up to the amount of the scholarship without the 10% penalty, though the earnings portion will still be taxed as income. You could also keep the money for grad school, change the beneficiary to a sibling or future grandchild, or roll up to $35,000 into your kid's Roth IRA over time if the account meets the 15-year rule. Talk to a tax preparer before withdrawing so the timing and paperwork line up with the scholarship year.
quick q, does my employer match count toward my 401k contribution limit

No, the employee contribution limit applies only to what you put in from your paycheck, so the match is on top of that. There is a higher overall limit covering both your money and your employer's, but most people never get close to it. Make sure you contribute at least enough to get the full match, because that's free money you can't get back later.
There's a guy on YouTube selling a $2,000 course that guarantees I retire in 5 years. Worth it?

Skip it, because nobody can guarantee investment results, and promises like that are a classic red flag. Everything that actually works for early retirement, like a high savings rate, low-cost index funds and tax-advantaged accounts, is freely available in library books and reputable sites. Put that $2,000 into your Roth IRA instead.
emergency fund in crypto? higher returns right

No, keep your emergency fund out of crypto. The whole point of this money is that it's there, at full value, the day your car dies or you lose your job, and crypto can drop 30 percent in a week. Put it in a high-yield savings account where it's FDIC-insured and earns a decent rate, and invest separately with money you won't need soon.
payday loan to cover rent this month, yes or no

No, unless you've truly exhausted everything else, because payday loans often carry effective annual rates of 300 percent or more and are built to roll over. Call your landlord first and ask for a short extension or a split payment, since many will agree if you reach out before the due date. Also dial 211 or search for emergency rental assistance in your area, and check whether a local credit union offers a small-dollar loan, which is far cheaper.
